title: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1
text:
In this tutorial, we try to create a table that is close to (Table 1 from the journal Treatment of Periodontal Disease and the Risk of Preterm Birth.
We start first by choosing the relevant columns to make Table 1.
As the final output looks complex, let’s break the task down to simpler tasks.

title: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1

Age, Race and Education Data
This task involves creating a summary table for age, race and number of years of education stratified by treatment group.
Here is the dataset required.

title: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1
text:
Using tbl_summary
Let’s try to build a summary table from opt_age_race_data using the default parameters of gtsummary::tbl_summary. We can see that table is giving a descriptive statistics of the overall population. It even display the statistics the patient ID.









include and by parameter
To exclude the patient ID being displayed, we set the parameter include a vector of column names to include in the summary table. To stratify the table by treatment group, we set the parameter by = "Group".










type parameter
Observe that the (continuous) variable Age is expressed as Median (Q1, Q3) while categorical variables are expressed as n (%). Variables with two categories (dichotomous) like White and Hisp are displayed differently to those with multiple categories like Education.
We can use the function gtsummary::assign_summary_type to identify the default summary type for each variable








On the other hand, the type parameter in the gtsummary::tbl_summary allows us to specify the summary type for each variable. The type parameter accepts a list of formulas as input.
Below is an example which we change the variable White and Black from dichotomous to categorical.










statistics parameter
Next, we need to ensure that - age is expressed in “means±SD”. - race and education is expressed in “no. (%)” (already done in default mode).
This can be achieved by using the statistic parameter which help users specify the statistics presented in the table. Like the type parameter, it accepts a list of formulas as input.
Below are some examples on how it can be done.

Variable NamesUse Helpers


Click on the different tabs.


We can list each variable individually as a character vector.










We can use all_ helper functions like gtsummary::all_continuous() and gtsummary::all_categorical() to make the code concise.











It can be observed that the displayed values {mean}±{sd} and {n} ({p}) are interpreted using glue::glue() syntax: a name that appears between curly brackets will be interpreted as a function name and the formatted result of that function will be placed in the table.
In gtsummary, some pre-calculated statistics available for display are
For categorical/dichotomous variable:

{n} for frequency.
{N} for denominator.
{p} for percent.

For continuous variable:

{median} for median.
{mean} for mean.
{sd} for standard deviation.
{min} for minimum.
{max} for maximum.
{p##} for percentile where ## is an integer from 0 to 100.For example, {p25} is the 25th percentile calculating using p25: quantile(probs=0.25, type=2).

A full list is provided here.
Feel free to experiment with the different statistics below.

Single LineMultiple Line


Click on the different tabs.












Sometimes, there may be a need to display continuous variables statistical summaries in multiple lines. To do that, you can change the variable type from continuous to continuous2.













Formatting in gtsummary
Before we get to the digits parameter, let’s take a look at some default formatting from gtsummary

style_number()style_sigfig()style_percent()style_ratio()style_pvalue()


Click on the different tabs.


gtsummary::style_number is the default style that gtsummary used internally to style the number. It rounds numbers to a fixed number of decimal places specified by the digits argument.








It has many flexible parameter to use and explore. The digits parameter can accept a vector of numbers to indicate how many decimal places to express for each number.










gtsummary::style_sigfig rounds numbers to a minimum number of significant figures (significant digits) via digits, adapting the decimal count dynamically depending on the magnitude of the number.








Unlike gtsummary::style_number, the digits parameter can only accept one number.










gtsummary::style_percent is the default style that gtsummary used internally to style percentages in proportions of categorical variables.
Observe that

All values are multiplied by 100.
Negative values are set to NA.
Positive numbers less than 0.1% are represented as <0.1.

Numbers less than 10% (exclusive) are rounded to digits + 1 places.











gtsummary::style_ratio is the default style that gtsummary used internally to format relative risk and odds ratio.
Observe that

Values between -1 and 1 will display digits number of significant digits based on gtsummary::style_sigfig.
Values greater than 1 (or less than -1) will display digits + 1 number of significant digits based on gtsummary::style_sigfig.











gtsummary::style_pvalue is the default style that gtsummary used internally to format p values.
Observe that

Values greater than 1 are set to NA.
Negative values are set to NA.
digits can only hold value 1, 2, or 3. It determines how many decimal places are presented.
High p values have a limit based on the value of digits.

When digits is 1, values more than 0.9 is represented as >0.9.
When digits is 2, values more than 0.99 is represented as >0.99.
When digits is 3, values more than 0.999 is represented as >0.999.

p values less than 0.001 are represented as <0.001.












Similar to the above style_*()functions, gtsummary has label_style_*() functions that takes the same inputs as the style_*()functions but returns a “wrapper” function that perform the styling.

label_style_number()label_style_sigfiglabel_style_percentlabel_style_ratiolabel_style_pvalue


Click on the different tabs.























































digits parameter
If we take a look at (Table 1 from the journal Treatment of Periodontal Disease and the Risk of Preterm Birth, the mean, standard deviation (sd) and percentage are expressed in 1 decimal place.
In gtsummary, we can specify the numerical format to display a given statistical result using the digits parameter. Though it accepts a list of formulas as input, it is also restricted based on what input is given to the statistic parameter.
Looking at the example below,

In the case of the statistic is {mean} ({sd}), passing the value 1 or c(1, 1) is the same as passing the output of gtsummary::label_style_number(digits=1) for both {mean} and {sd}.
In the case of the statistic is {n} ({p}), passing the value c(0, 1) is the same as passing the output of gtsummary::label_style_number(digits=0) for both {n} and gtsummary::label_style_percent(digits=1) for {p}.











label parameter
Currently, the column names of the dataset opt_age_race_data are used as the descriptive labels in the output table. We can update the descriptive labels printed using the label parameter. It accepts a list of formulas as input.
In the example below, we rename the following to match the (Table 1 in the publication.

Age to Age - yr.
Hisp to Hispanic.
Education to Education - no. (%).

title: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1
text:
Variable Group Header
You will observe in Table 1, there is a group header added above White, Black and Hispanic called Race or ethnic group - no. (%)". Unlike Education, we cannot create a categorical column Race or ethnic group - no. (%)" because some patients have mixed race/ethnicity (Both White and Hispanic).
Instead, we can use add_variable_group_header function in gtsummary to insert a custom section header row into a summary table and indents a chosen group of variables underneath it.
In the example below, we indicate the desired header name to the header parameter and the column names to group to the variables parameter.
crumbs: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1

title: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1
text:
p values
We then use gtsummary::add_p to add p values to tables created using gtsummary::tbl_summary.

Defaults hiddenDefaults explicit


Click on the different tabs.


By default based on the documentation, as

the by variable used (Group) in gtsummary::tbl_summary has two variables (Control and Treatment).
group variable in gtsummary::add_p is NULL (not doing paired t test).
adj.vars variable in gtsummary::add_p is NULL (not doing ANCOVA).
Each categorical groups to compare has at least 5 people.

Wilcoxon rank-sum test (wilcox.test) is applied to all continuous variables and Pearson’s Chi-squared Test for Count Data without continuity correction (chisq.test.no.correct) is applied to all categorical variables.
Also, the number of decimal place used for the p values by default is 1, hence we update the pvalue_fun input to gtsummary::label_style_pvalue(digits = 2).





















List of comparison tests that available within gtsummary or ways to create custom statistical tests can be found here.
crumbs: Building Age, Race and Education Summary for Table 1

text:
Remove footnotes
Finally, we use gtsummary::remove_footnote_header to remove any unnecessary footnote as this will be added in final stage.

title: HAT Workshop 20261021
text:
Preface
This workshop aims to introduce gtsummary by creating clinical summary tables using the Obstetrics and Periodontal Therapy Dataset from medicaldata. As the dataset is meant to be the source data for the journal Treatment of Periodontal Disease and the Risk of Preterm Birth, we try to create the tables such that it matches the table content (Table 1 and Table 2) from the paper as much as possible.

title: Cleaning Obstetrics and Periodontal Therapy Dataset
text:
In this section, we highlight in detail how the Obstetrics and Periodontal Therapy Dataset from R package medicaldata is prepared so that we can use gtsummary to create the clinical summary table.


The dataset can be obtain from medicaldata::opt.
The columns that we use are

PID: Participant ID.
Group: Randomized treatment assignment, factor.

“T” = Intervention.
“C” = Control.

Age: Age of participant at baseline (years), numeric.
Education: Education level of participant, factor.

“LT 8 yrs ” = Less than 8 years.
“8-12 yrs ” = 8 to 12 years.
“MT 12 yrs” = More than 12 years.
blank = Missing.

Black: Black participant (self-identified), factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
White: White participant (self-identified), factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Asian: Asian participant (self-identified), factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Nat.Am: Native American participant, incl. Latin Americans with aboriginal origin(self-identified), factor; “Yes”, “No”, “   ”.
Hisp: Hispanic participant (self-identified), factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
BMI: Body mass index, numeric.
Diabetes: Whether participant had diabetes at baseline (self-reported), factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Hypertension: Whether participant had chronic hypertension at baseline, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Drug.Add: Self-reported participant history of drug addiction, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Use.Alc: Self-reported participant history of alcohol use, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Use.Tob: Self-reported participant history of tobacco use, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ”.
Prev.preg: Any previous pregnancy, factor; “Yes”, “No ”.
Spont.ab: Previous spontaneous abortion, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ” = Missing or no previous pregnancies (Prev.preg = No).
Induced.ab: Previous induced abortion, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ” = Missing or no previous pregnancies (Prev.preg = No).
Any.stillbirth: Previous stillbirth, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ” = Missing or no previous pregnancies (Prev.preg = No).
Live.PTB: Previous live preterm birth for those with any previous pregnancy, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ” = Missing or no previous pregnancies (Prev.preg = No).
Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab: Any previous live pre-term birth, stillbirth, spontaneous abortion, or induced abortion, factor; “Yes”, “No ”, “   ” = Missing or no previous pregnancies (Prev.preg = No).
N.living.kids: Number of living children the subject had at baseline, numeric.
Birth.outcome: Birth outcome, factor,

“Elective abortion  ”.
“Live birth              ”.
“Lost to FU            ” = Lost to Follow-Up.
“Non-live birth      ” = Stillbirth or spontaneous abortion.

Preg.ended...37.wk: Whether the pregnancy ended before gestational age 37 weeks (259 days), factor, “Yes”; “No&nbsp”; “   ” = Lost to Follow-Up.
GA.at.outcome: Gestational age at end of pregnancy, or at mother’s last follow-up visit if lost to follow-up, numeric.
Birthweight: Infant birth weight at time of birth, abstracted from obstetrical records (grams), numeric.

We use stringr::str_trim to remove any whitespace in the factor columns.











Next, in the Group column, we rename C as Control and T as Treatment.











In the Education column, we rename LT 8 yrs as ≤8 yr, 8-12 yrs as 9-12 yr and MT 12 yrs as > 12 yr to match the labels as seen in Table 1.











In the Hisp column, we fill in the empty strings “” as No. We also convert Black, White, Asian, Nat.Am and Hisp to factors.











In the Hypertension column, we rename N as No and Y as Yes. In the Diabetes, Drug.Add, Use.Alc and Use.Tob columns, we convert “” to NA. We also convert Hypertension, Diabetes, Drug.Add, Use.Alc and Use.Tob to factors.











In the Spont.ab, Induced.ab, Any.stillbirth, Live.PTB and Any.live.ptb.sb.sp.ab.in.ab columns, we convert “” to NA
To match the labels as close as possible to Table 1, we let

have_living_child be No if N.living.kids is NA or 0 and Yes otherwise.
previous_live_preterm_birth be

NA if there is no previous pregnancy.
NA if there is previous pregnancy but number of living kids N.living.kids is NA and Live.PTB is No.
NA if there is previous pregnancy but number of living kids N.living.kids is NA and Live.PTB is NA.
NA if there is previous pregnancy but number of living kids N.living.kids is 0.
No if there is previous pregnancy, number of living kids N.living.kids is 1 to 9 and Live.PTB is No.
Yes if there is previous pregnancy, number of living kids N.living.kids is NA and Live.PTB is Yes.
Yes if there is previous pregnancy, number of living kids N.living.kids is 1 to 9 and Live.PTB is Yes.

Spont.ab be

NA if there is no previous pregnancy.
No if there is previous pregnancy, spontaneous abortion Spont.ab is NA or No.
Yes if there is previous pregnancy, spontaneous abortion Spont.ab is Yes.

Induced.ab be

NA if there is no previous pregnancy.
No if there is previous pregnancy, induced abortion Induced.ab is NA or No.
Yes if there is previous pregnancy, induced abortion Induced.ab is Yes.

Any.stillbirth be

NA if there is no previous pregnancy.
No if there is previous pregnancy, stillbirth Any.stillbirth is NA or No.
Yes if there is previous pregnancy, stillbirth Any.stillbirth is Yes.













We create the following new columns to identify those with pregnancy duration if less than 32, 35 and 37 weeks. - GA.at.outcome.weeks be the column GA.at.outcome divided by 7. - Preg_duration_32 be - Yes if GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 32. - No otherwise. - Preg_duration_35 be - Yes if GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 35. - No otherwise. - Preg_duration_37 be - Yes if GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 37. - No otherwise. - Preg_duration_37_regression be - 1 if GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 37. - 0 otherwise.











We create the following new columns to identify those with low birth weights. - Birthweight_2500 be - NA if Birthweight is NA. - Yes if Birthweight is less than 2500. - No otherwise. - Birthweight_2500_regression be - NA if Birthweight is NA. - 1 if Birthweight is less than 2500. - 0 otherwise. - Birthweight_1500 be - NA if Birthweight is NA. - Yes if Birthweight is less than 1500. - No otherwise.











We create the following new columns to identify those with pre-term live birth. - Recall GA.at.outcome.weeks is the column GA.at.outcome divided by 7. - Have_Live_Birth be - Yes if Birth.outcome is Live birth. - No otherwise. - Preterm_32 be - NA if Birth.outcome is Non-live birth. - Yes if Birth.outcome is Live birth and GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 32. - No otherwise. - Preterm_35 be - NA if Birth.outcome is Non-live birth. - Yes if Birth.outcome is Live birth and GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 35. - No otherwise. - Preterm_37 be - NA if Birth.outcome is Non-live birth. - Yes if Birth.outcome is Live birth and GA.at.outcome.weeks is less than 37. - No otherwise.









saveRDS(opt_data, file = here::here("data", "opt_data.rds"))
